Name: WordPress
Description: WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on the home page, nosniff header
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Large uploads and plugins can trigger WAF detections; they are only logged until you switch to Block. In WordPress set both addresses to https://your-domain.

Name: Nextcloud
Description: WebSocket on, WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /status.php
Note: A starting point, review it before use. WebDAV and large uploads pass through unchanged. In Nextcloud add this proxy to trusted_proxies and the domain to trusted_domains in config.php, and set overwriteprotocol to https.

Name: Home Assistant
Description: WebSocket on (required for the live UI), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Home Assistant refuses proxied requests until http: in configuration.yaml has use_x_forwarded_for: true and this proxy listed under trusted_proxies.

Name: Jellyfin
Description: WebSocket on, uptime monitor on /health, no WAF or rate limit changes
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Streaming makes many range requests, so no rate limit is set. Add this proxy under Known proxies in the Jellyfin network settings so client addresses are correct.

Name: Plex
Description: WebSocket on, uptime monitor on /identity, no WAF or rate limit changes
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Streaming makes many range requests, so no rate limit is set. In Plex add the public address under Network, Custom server access URLs.

Name: Grafana
Description: WebSocket on (Grafana Live), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /api/health
Note: A starting point, review it before use. In grafana.ini set root_url to the public https address. Grafana Live checks the Origin header, so add the address to live.allowed_origins if live panels fail.

Name: Vaultwarden
Description: WebSocket on (sync notifications), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /alive
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Set DOMAIN to the public https address in Vaultwarden. Restrict /admin with an access rule or a path rule if you enable the admin page.

Name: Gitea or GitLab
Description: WebSocket on, WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on the home page
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Git pushes over HTTPS send large bodies, which the WAF does not inspect past its limit. Set ROOT_URL (Gitea) or external_url (GitLab) to the public https address.

Name: Portainer
Description: WebSocket on (container console), WAF in detection mode, uptime monitor on /api/system/status
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Portainer controls your containers: also pick an access rule and an authentication provider. If it only serves HTTPS with its own certificate, turn on TLS for the upstream in the upstream settings.

Name: JSON API
Description: Rate limit 100 req/s per IP (burst 200), request id header, WAF in detection mode, WebSocket off
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Tune the rate limit to the real traffic of your clients. Set the health check path to an endpoint of your API.

Name: Static website
Description: Browser hardening headers, exploit blocking, light rate limit, WebSocket off
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Fits a site that only serves files. If the site uses WebSockets or is embedded in frames of other sites, adjust the result.

Name: Strict admin panel
Description: Rate limit 10 req/s per IP (burst 20), WAF in block mode, exploit blocking, browser hardening headers
Note: A starting point, review it before use. This preset does not turn on authentication by itself: choose an authentication provider and an access rule for the rule. The WAF can block legitimate admin actions, so watch the WAF log.

Name: Public website
Description: Rate limit 120 requests per minute per IP
Note: A starting point, review it before use. Enable a rate limit on every public site: 120 requests per minute per client IP (a burst of 120 is allowed, then 2 per second). Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: Login page
Description: Strict limit of 5 requests per minute per IP on /login, /signin, /wp-login.php and /auth
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 5 attempts per minute per IP (burst 5) on the usual login paths; the rest of the site is not limited by this preset. Add other login paths under Path rules. Account-level protection is needed in the app itself (lockout, MFA, password policy): an attacker with many addresses is not slowed down by a per IP limit. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: Admin dashboard
Description: Rate limit 60 requests per minute per IP, needs a login
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 60 requests per minute per client IP. Prefer a VPN or an IP restriction (an access rule) for admin dashboards; a rate limit is not a replacement for either. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: Odoo ERP
Description: Rate limit 300 requests per minute per IP with bursts, 10 per minute on /web/login, WebSocket cap
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 300 requests per minute per client IP with a burst of 600, because Odoo loads many small requests. Tune it by endpoint under Path rules (for example reports and imports). /web/login is limited to 10 per minute (burst 5): account-level protection is needed in Odoo (for example the Auth Signup and login attempt modules, MFA). Odoo live chat and bus use WebSockets: handshakes are not counted in the request limit and each client is capped at 100 connections. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: REST API per key
Description: Rate limit 120 requests per minute per API key (Authorization header), per IP when there is none
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 120 requests per minute per client, where the client is the Authorization header (hashed in memory, never logged); a request without one is counted per IP. To key by another header such as X-API-Key, change the key in the Rate limit card. A per IP guard of 10 times the limit stops clients from inventing keys. Prefer API-key based limits to IP based ones, but keys must be issued and checked by the API itself. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: Webhook receiver
Description: Rate limit 120 requests per minute per source IP with a burst of 240
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 120 requests per minute per source IP with a burst of 240, because senders deliver in bursts. Authenticate webhooks in the app (verify the signature or secret token of every delivery); a rate limit does not tell a genuine sender from a forged one. If the sender publishes its addresses, restrict the site to them with an access rule. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: File upload
Description: Limit of 15 requests per minute per IP on /upload, /uploads and /api/upload (POST, PUT)
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 15 upload requests per minute per client IP (burst 5), separate from any general limit of the site. Adjust the paths to your app under Path rules. The limit counts requests, not bytes, and per IP rather than per user unless users sit behind one address. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: WebSocket app limits
Description: WebSocket on, at most 20 concurrent connections per IP, handshakes not counted in the request limit
Note: A starting point, review it before use. WebSockets are limited by the number of concurrent connections per client IP (20), not by the HTTP request limit: a handshake is not counted against it and frames inside a connection are never counted. Raise the cap when many users share one address. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.

Name: Monitoring-friendly
Description: Rate limit 300 requests per minute per IP, uptime monitor on
Note: A starting point, review it before use. 300 requests per minute per client IP, enough for frequent polling. Zoraxy cannot know your monitoring system: add its addresses (or a secret header) under Rate limit, Trusted monitoring, so that checks are never limited at all. Rate limiting protects availability, not accounts; the numbers are starting points, adjust them from the 429 count in the statistics.
